mechanism: Primidone increases vitamin B6 metabolism and decreases pyridoxal phosphate (active form) concentrations, potentially reducing B6-dependent enzymatic functions and increasing seizure risk.
action: Monitor vitamin B6 levels and consider B6 supplementation (typically 25-50 mg daily) in patients on chronic primidone therapy; watch for signs of B6 deficiency including peripheral neuropathy and worsening seizure control.
